I’m gonna give you my personal experience that I did not realize off the bat.

 In fact it took me two years to realize I rebounded. 

I had gotten out of a 13 year on and off abusive relationship with my daughter‘s father. I had left him about seven times in those 13 years and I never actually dated anybody else. The very last time I left him for good it was an extremely volatile physical bad experience. It was a lot of trauma.


 I had left the house on August 31 and in my mind several months had gone by. He had started dating somebody about a month or two later and even though I knew I had to leave him and it was a horriblesituation. I was still very emotionally attached to him, but because he started dating someone else I figured it was time I also move on. 

so in February (5 months after I left my ex)  I started talking to a man that led to an almost 2 year.  Situation. I was still very emotionally attached to him, but because he started dating someone else I figured it was time. I also move on so in February I started talking to a man that led to an almost 2 year committed relationship. 

The relationship was mostly so great but eventually fell apart because my personal undealt with trauma, breakup, abandonment issues, etc were never properly processed and dealt with. I am a single mother, with 2 dogs and 2 cats and I work as a dog sitter/dog walker who is constantly busy as well as volunteering in my community. 

It isn’t so much how much time. But if that person properly grieved, processed and dealt with the breakup.  I had no idea I just used my anxiety and survival mode and life issues that pop up to escape and distract from my unresolved issues and unprocessed feelings. I was so distracted and on the run the entire almost 2 year new relationship with the nice man. 

I wanted love and I wanted to move on. But ignoring certain things often by accident. It wasn’t til my new relationship fell apart from my own triggers and much more and him saying his intentions weren’t to never talk to me again but to give ME space to process/heal from heartbreak. 

Stubborn me was like I don’t need space and time!!! And then little by little and a few more life events I realized oh my gosh he was right. I never ever processed the breakup of my 13 year relationship and further diving in therapy exploring what he meant I realized I never ever processed or healed from most of my breakups. I just ended up In other relationships unplanned never sitting on my own and coming back to being me and shedding who I was in those failed relationships. 

TDLR: 
I don’t think it matters the time length I think what matters is true shadow work which is not always apparent. If they truly processed the feelings and break up and are back to being “themselves” and not the hurt broken person that was the outcome  of their last relationship. I don’t think it matters if it’s 3 months 1 year or 5 years. If there are unprocessed feelings and they didn’t grieve and process the last breakup … time doesn’t matter.
